items.title: World Bank's $100 billion crisis cushion
items.summary: Bangkok: The World Bank is in discussions with 30 to 40 countries about potential crisis aid to help them manage energy shocks and price increases triggered by the war in the Middle East, its president, Ajay Banga, told Reuters in an interview.Banga said the global economy had proven fairly resilient, in part due to big AI investments and adjustments in supply and demand for oil, which meant that few countries had sought the initial $25 billion in crisis funds that the World Bank had made available when the war began in late February.Also Read: World Bank raises India FY27 growth forecast to 7.1%, flags oil, El Niño risksHowever, a sharp spike in diesel and fertilizer prices and other factors, including the looming super El Nino weather effect, were adding to challenges facing developing countries, Banga said in an interview ahead of this week's annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank."There is pressure, and so I think maybe over the coming months, more countries will come for some slice of that first $50 to $60 billion," Banga said, referring to the initial $25 billion plus another $35 billion that countries could tap by diverting resources from already approved World Bank projects."We'll see, but we're ready. We're engaged. We're having conversations with a number of them, you know, 30 to 40 countries are in dialogue with us," he said.Many developing countries have been hit hard by the spike in energy prices and high interest rates that have increased borrowing costs at a time when their fiscal coffers are still depleted by measures taken during the COVID-19 pandemic and the spike in inflation following Russia's invasion of Ukraine.World Bank estimates show that developing countries owe external creditors about $400 billion in 2026, with interest payments alone comprising one-third of the total.Banga said more countries had shown interest in retooling existing projects than in tapping the immediate crisis window to address their liquidity needs. If the situation worsened, the Bank could make available as much as $100 billion in funds, he said, exceeding the $70 billion disbursed during the pandemic.The World Bank last month announced that it attracted a record $112 billion in private capital in the year ended June versus $69 billion a year earlier, and more than triple the 2022 total before Banga, a former Mastercard CEO, became president.Also Read: World Bank mobilises $112 billion in private capital for developing nationsThat was on top of the $123 billion invested from the bank's own resources for that year, for a combined $235 billion, Banga said, underscoring the importance of tapping all available resources, especially at a time when Western countries have sharply cut official bilateral development aid."There is no one answer that fits when the world has these kinds of issues. What you need to do is figure out how to cut your coat to suit your cloth," Banga said.Banga said he expected further gains in private capital flows in coming years, aided by expanded political risk guarantees from the bank's Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency, growth in local currency financing, and continued work on regulatory reforms that made it easier for foreign investors.The private capital jump was biggest in projects in upper-middle-income countries like Argentina or India, which accounted for $50 billion of the private capital, and lower-middle-income countries including Bangladesh and Angola, which accounted for $37 billion. But more work was needed to boost the roughly $3 billion in private capital flowing to low-income countries."In the smaller countries, it hasn't multiplied enough, and there are challenges," he said, noting the bank would announce some new initiatives this week aimed at ensuring micro-, small- and medium-sized businesses also had access to private capital.Banga said private capital growth was also regionally spread, with the largest increase seen in Latin America and the Caribbean, which accounted for $36.3 billion of last year's total, followed by Europe and Central Asia with $21.3 billion, South Asia with $19.2 billion and Africa with $22 billion.The top 10 recipient countries were Brazil, India, Turkey, Romania, Nigeria, Argentina, South Africa, Bangladesh, Mexico and Chile, the Bank said.Banga said the World Bank and IMF were working together to address the high debt levels plaguing many developing countries through a series of initiatives, including efforts to boost countries' domestic revenue collections.The Bank had already set up some debt-for-development swaps for Angola and Ivory Coast, and a portfolio-based guarantee for Argentina, and was working on over a dozen more projects."We've got 14 or 15 in the pipeline, helping them rotate out higher-priced old debt for newer-priced debt with our guarantees," with the difference then targeted at education, healthcare, water, or nature programs, he said.

items.summary: Kathmandu: A debris-laden flash flood in a river has swept away more than 35 houses and bridges in Nepal's Gorkha district on Sunday, authorities said, urging people living along the stream to move to higher ground.The flood in the Budhi Gandaki River swept away houses in Salleri, Paiyuka and the riverbed at Jagat, as well as a suspension bridge connecting the ward, Ram Kumar Gurung, ward chair of Chumnubri Rural Municipality-3, was quoted as saying by the Kathmandu Post.Also Read: Nepal floods: 1,453 dead, nearly 5,300 still missing a month after disasterDharmendra Kumar Mishra, Gorkha's chief district officer, said preliminary reports indicated that a landslide had occurred above Siuribas. No casualties have been reported so far, he said.The cause of the sudden surge remained unclear. Residents suspect that the Syar stream, a tributary of the Budhi Gandaki between Lokpa and Chumling in Chumnubri-6, may have been blocked, triggering the flood.The flash flood in the river swept away more than 35 houses in several locations in northern Gorkha, officials said.Also Read: Nepal wraps up Rasuwa flood search; shifts focus to rehabilitation, reconstructionChumnubri Rural Municipality Deputy Chair Laxmi Gurung said the flood that hit the Budhi Gandaki this morning is reminiscent of the Bhotekoshi flood in Rasuwa, Online Khabar news portal reported."The Budhigandaki flood is reminiscent of the Bhotekoshi flood," she said. "It has washed away dozens of houses. It is not possible to say the exact extent of the damage right now."The devastating flooding struck the Bhote Koshi River in Rasuwa district on August 26. The floods in the Rasuwa and Trishuli river areas claimed 1,455 lives, while 5,285 people remained missing, according to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA).Home Minister Sudan Gurung said the flood had also swept away the bridge linking Nyakchet and Philim bazaar in Chumnubri-3. With the river continuing to rise, helicopters had been deployed for rescue operations, relief distribution and evacuations, he said.Nepal Police, the Armed Police Force and local authorities were mobilised to carry out rescue and relief operations."The flood came early in the morning, and we could not even take out our belongings," Ram Kumar said."Everyone fled as soon as we heard the flood was coming." The full extent of the damage was not yet known, he said.Residents in riverside settlements, including Chumling and Lokpa, fled their homes after hearing loud roaring sounds from the streams from around 4am. Tourists staying at local hotels also fled, residents said.Sherap Gurung, a resident of Lokpa, said the sound suggested that the water flow had repeatedly stopped and resumed."Because it was dark, we could not tell whether the stream had been blocked or a landslide had occurred. It had not rained either," he said.Authorities were using loudspeakers to warn people living along the river and urge them to move to safer locations.

items.title: India condemns attack on Saudi airport that killed 12, injured over 300
items.summary:
India on Sunday strongly condemned a major attack on Saudi Arabia's international airport in Riyadh that killed 12 people and injured over 300.
New Delhi said the repeated attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure in the Gulf nation are "completely unacceptable and must cease immediately."
"We strongly condemn the repeated attacks on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport over the past few days, including the dastardly attack on October 10, which have led to loss of lives, injuries and damage to property," the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said in a statement.
"We express our condolences to the families of the deceased and wish speedy recovery to the injured persons," it said.
Saudi Arabia has blamed Houthi militants for the attack.
"We stand in solidarity with the people and the government of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in defence of their sovereignty, and hope that peace and normalcy returns to the region at the earliest," the MEA said.

Mystery surrounds death of young worker in Russia studying deadly diseases
items.summary:
The World Health Organisation (WHO) said Saturday it still doesn't know what caused the death of a young worker at a lab in Russia that focuses on plague and other illnesses.
The UN health agency has cited initial, unconfirmed reports suggesting pneumonic plague, a severe disease less common than the better-known bubonic plague linked to the Black Death in the Middle Ages. Pneumonic plague spreads from person to person, causing a severe form of pneumonia, but recovery rates are high if it is detected and treated in time.
WHO, in its first full Disease Outbreak News since the case emerged earlier this month, called for a continued investigation.
Russian health officials, it said, had conducted more than 5,500 tests and found no evidence of any dangerous pathogenic microorganisms.
"Additional clinical, epidemiological and laboratory information, including confirmation of the diagnosis in the deceased laboratory worker, is required to improve confidence in the assessment," WHO said.

items.summary: After saying he deserved to be disciplined, Portugal's Cristiano Ronaldo got what he asked for Saturday when he provisionally was suspended by his national team.The Portuguese Football Federation opened disciplinary proceedings against the team captain after he walked out of camp during the just-completed international break following a miscommunication with head coach Jorge Jesus.In a letter that was revealed this week, Ronaldo said he was told by Jesus he would be used as a substitute in a Nations League match against Norway. Ronaldo warmed up along the sideline but did not see playing time.Before the following match against Denmark, the 41-year-old striker departed camp after notifying the federation he was leaving."Disciplinary proceedings have been initiated against Cristiano Ronaldo dos Santos Aveiro, following a decision by the Non-Professional Section on October 9, 2026," the Portuguese Football Federation said in a statement.Ronaldo already has returned to his club team, Al Nassr in Saudi Arabia, and scored a goal in a 3-0 victory over Diriyah on Friday.In his explanation of his actions, Ronaldo admitted that his decision to leave camp was not the best way to handle the situation. But he added that Jesus "broke his word" on more than one occasion."I owe my national team teammates an apology for leaving the training camp," Ronaldo said. "Despite the absolute breach of trust in the coach's word, as anyone who witnessed our conversations can testify, I should not have done it. The responsibility is exclusively mine."After just participating in his sixth World Cup for Portugal this past summer, Ronaldo said he is open to discipline. According to reports, the federation's regulations call for a suspension of anywhere from a month to six months for a player who "abandons" national team activity."The consequence of my actions should be assessed and punished by the (federation)," Ronaldo said. "The punishment should not have any mitigating circumstances. I am not just any player; I am the captain of the team, and that constitutes an aggravating factor."After playing in 234 matches for his national team, while scoring 146 goals, Ronaldo said he still has the desire to play for Portugal in the future. Portugal has Nations League matches scheduled against Denmark and Wales next month.

Trump’s AI liability push opens blame game
items.summary: The Trump administration’s embrace of legal liability to enforce artificial intelligence safety sets the stage for future conflicts over who foots the bill when AI models go rogue: the companies that design the systems or the people that deploy the technology.Holding AI developers financially responsible for the safety of their products has won support from Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and former White House AI czar David Sacks, who argue that existing liability laws would be more effective than new rules. President Donald Trump, in spurning new AI safeguards, has taken it a step further, saying the Justice Department should intervene if models get out of hand.In a sign of the administration’s increased willingness to invoke current law to address safety concerns, Trump’s newly launched AI task force late Friday warned developers that they are required to report and resolve security incidents or face potential unspecified consequences.“Companies must immediately disclose incidents involving their models and follow with swift, decisive action to remedy any and all harm,” the group dubbed the Super Intelligence Force said in a statement following the disclosure of a breach by Anthropic PBC. “Delayed notification, inadequate corrective action, and a failure to take responsibility will not be tolerated.”Yet the administration’s reliance on liability as a cornerstone of AI safety remains riddled with uncertainties. Existing cybersecurity and product liability laws may not be strong enough for the federal government to hold AI agents accountable for harm, legal experts say.Even when there are clear victims, there are few legal precedents to define who’s on the hook for damages caused by rogue agents and how careful companies have to be when developing their AI tools. Further complicating any finding of responsibility, a model’s behavior is shaped by both its AI industry developer and the end user deploying the system.“Despite calls for liability, it remains unsettled whether AI companies are legally responsible for securing their models against contributing to any harm, or whether users share legal responsibility for what they instruct those models to do,” said Ben Hayum, a tech and national security-focused research assistant at the Center for a New American Security.Questions about who’s liable for AI gone awry have taken on new urgency with the rapid adoption of the technology by businesses across the economy. Wall Street firms, retailers and airlines are deploying AI agents and tools in a widening range of operations from customer service to invoice processing. The outcome of that debate could upend the pace of adoption as well as the upcoming Wall Street debuts of the two AI leaders, OpenAI and Anthropic.When relying on AI agents, end users often entrust the system to perform a task without giving it specific directions how to complete the work. That raises the possibility that AI agents could make choices the user hasn’t vetted, including potentially harmful actions. In those cases, it’s unclear who would be at fault: the company that developed the tool, or the user employing it.The administration’s liability push fits into Trump’s largely hands-off approach toward regulating AI, a technology whose growth is central to his economic agenda. Last week, after hosting nearly two dozen Silicon Valley leaders at the White House, Trump reiterated his desire for the AI industry to police itself while unveiling a nonbinding accord for companies to adopt stricter internal controls.At the same time, Friday’s announcement warning companies about the need to disclose problems with their models suggests that the White House is willing to use this newly formed AI group  — led by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, along with Federal Trade Commission Chairman Andrew Ferguson, Office of Personnel Management chief Scott Kupor and Emil Michael, the Pentagon’s chief technology officer — as an enforcer of existing statutes.Debate over how to mitigate AI risks has accelerated following a spate of alarming breaches along with a now-viral essay from Anthropic Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei that warned of the technology’s catastrophic risks. Amodei and other AI leaders have called for additional government regulation and industrywide coordination to help mitigate the risks, prompting some pushback from other tech and policy officials.Unlikely allies Nvidia Corp. CEO Jensen Huang and former FTC Chair Lina Khan have argued for robust use of existing laws to prevent the dire outcomes that AI safety advocates warn about. At the same time, Khan has criticized having industry police itself, calling it “a recipe for disaster” and indicating there’s room for future AI legislation.For Trump and his allies, threats of legal action are aimed at spurring developers like OpenAI and Anthropic into ensuring their systems run safely. During a congressional hearing last month, Bessent rejected the idea of new rules as well as any notion that AI labs should be spared liability exposure. “The best way to guarantee safety is that the creators are liable for what they build and generate,” he said.Sacks has repeated the phrase “mother of all product liability lawsuits” to describe the consequences he thinks should await AI companies that fail to make safe products.The US government has already taken a step toward making that approach a reality. The FTC is now scrutinizing OpenAI, Anthropic and other AI companies about product safety, following several high-profile cybersecurity incidents, including a swarm of OpenAI agents breaching Hugging Face Inc., a repository for open-source software.The FTC probe sets the stage for officials to jawbone the companies making AI models into more intense self-regulation. It tees up a legal threat for the developers who signed the voluntary accord with Trump last week that recommended they adopt outside safety auditing and tweak their board structures to deal with safety risks.If the Justice Department, as Trump has floated, moved to prosecute companies for rogue AI hacks, many of those cases would hinge on the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act, or CFAA, a decades-old law that requires prosecutors to prove that a plaintiff intended to hack a system. That standard will be difficult to meet in cases of unintended AI agent behavior.“AI agents could engage in conduct that would be a tort or even a crime for a human, and yet no one could be liable under current law,” Gabriel Weil, a professor at the University of Houston Law Center and senior fellow at the Institute for Law & AI, said during a New York City Council meeting Monday. Weil added that negligence and product liability arguments currently apply to such incidents, though those approaches also have limitations.In a Senate hearing last week, Paul Ohm, a Georgetown University law professor who’s set to publish a textbook on AI law, said it might be possible for developers to be held liable under the FTC’s product liability authority but warned that the CFAA currently requires intent — something typically only attributed to humans — meaning AI agents may be off the hook for now.Two US lawmakers are trying to change that. Senator Josh Hawley, a Missouri Republican, and Senator Chris Murphy, a Connecticut Democrat, plan to introduce legislation that would change the CFAA to make AI developers civilly and criminally liable for failing to impose reasonable safeguards on a model’s hacking capabilities.Existing law does allow victims of rogue incidents to pursue tort liability lawsuits, but those cases are limited because they would likely require a defendant to show that AI companies failed to provide reasonable care — an intentionally abstract duty companies would likely try to argue they fulfilled. In addition, “tort law reaches its limit once the responsible company is bankrupt,” Weil said, meaning it may not offer protection against civilization-level risks.A California nonprofit is testing what kind of accountability is possible under existing law with a lawsuit against OpenAI over the Hugging Face breach that seeks a court order barring the company’s AI agents from accessing third-party systems without permission. The case, filed under the state’s data security law, also seeks to prohibit OpenAI from continuing any unsafe AI development that poses a public risk.“We haven’t seen how a court will answer the question, but the idea that technology manufacturers are going to somehow fully get away from being liable for harm that their tech causes or abets seems super far fetched,” said Michael Pastor, the dean for tech law programs at New York Law School.Representative Lori Trahan, a Massachusetts Democrat, released a draft Wednesday of legislation that would erase some of that ambiguity by holding AI developers responsible for harm even if they used reasonable care when making an agent or model. Her bill would also bar companies from arguing that their AI agents lack human intent.Without legislation, it will likely take years for courts to apply precedent to new AI scenarios, Pastor said. That leaves the door open for developers and end users to quibble over who’s responsible when the technology causes harm, and there are signs that those sides have already begun to form.Sacks, whose venture capital portfolio includes startups that deploy AI models as end users, and Huang, who maintains more pricing power over the chips he sells when AI developers face more competitive pressure, are both advocating for maximum responsibility falling to the developers.Meanwhile AI developers, including OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Anthropic’s Amodei, have pushed for mandatory pre-deployment testing, a move that could shift some responsibility onto a government testing apparatus alongside their companies.For now, the legal underpinning for software-related liability remains underdeveloped compared to other fields, said Julia Powles, a professor at the UCLA School of Law. That’s because sustained lobbying by the tech industry has sought to “ensure that software is regulated by contract — terms of service and end-user license agreements – instead of by tort, crime, and consumer protection.”“The same tech actors that have created deep dependencies in digital infrastructure are now recklessly accelerating cybersecurity threats to that very infrastructure — and then disclaiming responsibility for the resulting chaos,” Powles said. “There’s precious little space for the public in all these debates because the whole chess board has been set up by industry.”

items.title: India slams UN for 'unwarranted interference'
items.summary: India on Saturday rejected the United Nations’ concerns over the detention of protesters in Delhi, calling the remarks “misplaced” and an “unwarranted interference in the internal affairs of India”.The response came after the UN called for the immediate and unconditional release of all those it described as “arbitrarily detained” during protests in the national capital.Follow ET's LIVE coverage of the CJP protests in Delhi here— UNHumanRights (@UNHumanRights) The UN expressed concern over reports of mass detentions of demonstrators, protest leaders, members of civil society organisations, lawyers and journalists before and during large-scale demonstrations in Delhi.“We call on the authorities to ensure that the right to peaceful assembly is fully respected and fulfilled,” it said.India invokes constitutional safeguards, questions UN’s impartialityThe Permanent Mission of India to the UN said the right to peaceful assembly was guaranteed by the Constitution and safeguarded by robust institutions, an independent judiciary and a free media. It added that, as in every democracy, citizens exercised this right subject to reasonable restrictions in the interest of public order.“The authorities, for their part, act in accordance with the law, and our courts remain available to all for redressal of any grievances,” the mission said in a statement reiterated by the Ministry of External Affairs.India also urged the UN human rights office to apply its mandate impartially. “In this context, OHCHR would also do well to devote comparable attention to large-scale protests elsewhere, consistent with its mandate of impartiality and non-selectivity,” the statement said.Also read: Delhi CJP Protest Today: What's happening at Jantar Mantar? Here's what we know so far— IndiaUNGeneva (@IndiaUNGeneva) Over 7,000 detained as Opposition protests sweep DelhiThe UN’s remarks followed protests led by Opposition parties and the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), which demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the withdrawal of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. More than 7,000 protesters were detained, including CJP leader Abhijit Dipke, four former chief ministers and YouTuber Dhruv Rathee.Several INDIA bloc leaders, including former chief ministers Arvind Kejriwal, Mamata Banerjee, Pinarayi Vijayan and Manik Sarkar, were detained at multiple locations across the capital as they attempted to join the CJP-led protest.Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said the capital would not be held hostage and accused Opposition leaders Rahul Gandhi and Kejriwal of trying to turn the city into a “battleground” in league with their “B-Team”, the CJP.Journalists also alleged that they were detained despite displaying their press identity cards. Some claimed police personnel seized their official phones before taking them to detention buses alongside other protesters. Videos circulating on social media showed journalists displaying their press identity cards from inside the buses.

King Khalid International Airport has been targeted multiple times this week, with three Saudi civilians including a pilot killed on Thursday.
Iran-backed Houthi rebels in neighbouring Yemen have claimed responsibility for those attacks. There was no immediate Houthi statement Saturday.
The airport issued a terse alert telling passengers to check with airlines to confirm flights before going there.

items.summary:
The National Investigation Agency (NIA) has registered a case to probe last month's mid-air cockpit attack on Captain Smit Machchhar aboard a flydubai flight, officials said on Saturday.
The case has been registered under the relevant provisions of the Anti-Hijacking Act, 2016, and the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967, they said.
Indian national pilot Machchhar was stabbed and seriously injured by his co-pilot in the cockpit of flydubai flight FZ1073, while travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv on September 30 "in an apparent attempt to hijack or cause it to crash," the officials said, citing an FIR registered by the NIA on October 9.

items.title: Tahir Hussain convicted in 2020 Delhi riots case; 12 others acquitted
items.summary:
A court here on Saturday convicted former AAP councillor Tahir Hussain in a case related to the 2020 northeast Delhi riots in the Dayalpur area, while acquitting the 12 other accused.
Additional Sessions Judge Praveen Singh convicted Hussain under Indian Penal Code (IPC) Section 147 (punishment for rioting) read with Section 109 (Punishment of abetment if the act abetted is committed in consequence and where no express provision is made for its punishment).
The court listed the matter for hearing arguments on quantum of sentence on November 16.
The 13 accused in the case included Hussain, Mohammad Shadab, Shah Alam, Riyasat Ali, Gulfam, Rashid, Mohammad Rihan, Mohammad Abid, Arshad Qayyum, Irshad Ahmed, Deepak Singh Saini, Navneet and Mehak Singh.
They were accused of rioting, theft in a dwelling house, mischief by fire or explosive substances, among other offences.
In July, a Delhi court convicted Hussain and four others in the case related to the killing of Intelligence Bureau .

A Delhi court on Saturday dismissed a criminal defamation complaint filed by Delhi minister Parvesh Verma against Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leader Saurabh Bharadwaj.
Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate (ACJM) Neha Mittal declined to take cognisance of the complaint.
She said that the imputations attributed to Bharadwaj were in the nature of questions and did not amount to defamation. A detailed order is awaited.
Verma had alleged that Bharadwaj made certain malicious and false posts on social media.
He claimed that Bharadwaj's statements linking him to a POCSO Act case related to an incident in a school in his former constituency of West Delhi damaged his reputation.
Bharadwaj and Verma have made allegations against each other ever since the latter slapped an AAP supporter in full public view during a road inspection in the Vikaspuri area after charges of shoddy public work.

Negative global sentiment overshadowed these positive signals.However, JioBlackRock Mutual Fund said the correction has brought the market to levels where the risk-reward equation appears more attractive. The Nifty recorded an eight-week losing streak, its longest since 2001, and entered an oversold zone based on its weekly Relative Strength Index (RSI). The fund house also highlighted technical support around the 200-week exponential moving average and a support cluster between 22,000 and 22,400.Crude oil prices, which had surged to $108 a barrel, subsequently cooled to around $95, offering some relief. At the same time, FII net short positions in index futures remained elevated at approximately 267,000 contracts, potentially providing additional momentum to a market rally if short-covering gathers pace.Despite these supportive technical factors, the fund house cautioned that a sustained recovery is far from certain. Global and domestic macroeconomic conditions remain challenging, and corporate fundamentals and growth are uneven across stocks and sectors.Against this backdrop, JioBlackRock Mutual Fund expects tactical allocations to be important for investors seeking potential returns. It also sees hybrid fund categories as relatively more attractive in the current environment.What should debt mutual fund investors do?In fixed income, JioBlackRock Mutual Fund expects elevated bond yields to persist as inflationary pressures, crude oil prices and expectations around Reserve Bank of India (RBI) policy influence the market.India’s 10-year government security yield rose from around 6.9% at the end of August to above 7.15%, amid expectations of an RBI rate hike at the Monetary Policy Committee’s October meeting. Consumer price inflation rose to 4.82% in August, marking the third consecutive month above the RBI’s 4% target.The fund house noted that rising inflation, rupee weakness, higher crude prices and strong economic growth could give the RBI greater room to respond than it would have in a weaker growth environment. The narrowing yield differential between India and the US also complicates the outlook, with potential implications for foreign portfolio flows and the currency.Liquidity remains another concern. Earlier inflows had pushed surplus banking system liquidity to Rs 11.16 lakh crore. The RBI subsequently reduced the surplus through measures including variable rate reverse repo operations, open market operation sales and foreign exchange interventions.However, the fund house said liquidity pressures could persist as advance-tax outflows return to the system and investors assess the possibility of more structural liquidity withdrawal.Also Read | Parag Parikh Flexi Cap Fund added DLF, Bharti Airtel, Indus Towers and 10 other stocks to its portfolio in September. Details hereGiven uncertainty over interest rates and the direction of the bond market, JioBlackRock Mutual Fund said duration timing remains a low-conviction trade. Instead, it sees the current yield curve as offering a relatively attractive opportunity to lock in elevated yields across maturities.For investors with defined investment horizons, target maturity funds could help lock in prevailing yields. Explained: How mutual fund SIPs harness the power of compounding to build wealth
items.summary: Compounding is one of the most effective ways to build long-term wealth. When paired with Systematic Investment Plans (SIPs) in mutual funds, it allows investors to grow their money over time through regular investments and reinvested returns. This approach can help them work towards key financial goals, from retirement planning and buying a home to funding a child’s education.What is compounding?Compounding lets investors earn returns not only on their initial investment but also on gains they've accumulated over time. This creates a snowball effect, as those returns generate further gains. The longer the money stays invested, the greater the potential benefit.Also Read |Parag Parikh Flexi Cap Fund added DLF, Bharti Airtel, Indus Towers and 10 other stocks to its portfolio in September. Details here How SIPs harness the power of compoundingSIP is a disciplined way to invest a fixed amount regularly—monthly, quarterly, or even weekly—in a mutual fund scheme. While SIPs help average out market volatility through rupee cost averaging, their true magic lies in how they make compounding work more efficiently over time.By investing consistently through SIPs, even small amounts can grow significantly due to the compounding effect. Each SIP instalment earns returns, and those returns are reinvested and continue to earn more. The longer you stay invested, the more the compounding effect multiplies your wealth.Example: Power of compoundingYou start a SIP of Rs 10,000 per month, and the mutual fund gives an average annual return of 12%. You plan to invest for 20 years.The yearly SIP investment - Rs 10,000 × 12 months = Rs 1,20,000 per yearThe total investment period -  20 yearsRs 1,20,000 × 20 = Rs 24,00,000The maturity amount after 20 years at 12% return using SIP compound interest formula or calculator = Rs 99,90,000 (approximately Rs1 crore)Amount you invested: Rs 24,00,000Wealth created through compounding: Rs 75,90,000% of return through compounding: approximately 76% of the total maturity valueHere, compounding has worked quietly in the background, helping you build more than four times your actual investment.Also Read |ET Alpha Wealth Summit 2.0: REITs can diversify portfolios, but total returns matter, says Ramesh NairWhy time matters more than the amount you investMany investors delay investing because they think they need a large amount to begin. But with compounding, time in the market matters more than timing the market. Starting early—even with a small SIP—can yield better results than starting late with a larger amount.How to maximise the benefits of compounding through SIPsThe most important thing to do for compounding through SIPs is to start early, as the earlier you begin, the more time your money has to grow. Secondly, one should stay consistent, which means not stopping SIPs due to short-term market volatility.Thirdly, stay invested for the long term because compounding rewards patience. Lastly, increase the SIP amount over time, which means gradually raising your SIP as your income grows to enhance your corpus.SIPs are one of the most convenient and effective ways to benefit from the power of compounding. They make market investing simple for everyone—from beginners to seasoned investors. By starting early, staying invested, and being consistent, you can put compounding to work and create meaningful wealth over time.One should always remember that it's not just how much you invest, but how long you stay invested that truly makes the difference.(Disclaimer: Recommendations, suggestions, views and opinions given by the experts are their own. The demonstration is aimed at demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and opposing the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise. Police have detained more than 150 people, while restrictions on Metro services, internet access and road traffic have affected movement across parts of the national capital.Delhi protest: Dhruv Rathee among those detainedYouTuber Dhruv Rathee has been detained by Delhi Police from his residence in Sector 56, Gurugram, sources told news agency PTI.The Cockroach Janta Party also claimed on X that Rathee had been detained, alleging that the government was afraid of young people who questioned its actions.CJP's legal head Ratna Singh was also reportedly detained from her Delhi residence, according to media reports.Meanwhile, police detained more than 200 protesters on Saturday morning ahead of the planned demonstration. Earlier, a few protesters who had started gathering at Jantar Mantar were also detained.The detentions came amid heightened security arrangements across Delhi, with police checking vehicles at border points and deploying personnel at key locations to prevent unauthorised gatherings.Nitin Nabin accuses INDIA bloc, CJP of trying to destabilise IndiaBJP president Nitin Nabin accused the INDIA bloc, led by Rahul Gandhi, and the CJP of attempting to create instability in the country.In his remarks, Nabin described the two groups as anarchic and alleged that they were competing to create unrest instead of accepting the public's electoral verdict. He further alleged that their political activities were being carried out at the behest of foreign forces, but did not provide evidence for the claim in the quoted remarks.— ANI (@ANI) Nabin also said India was progressing despite global crises and accused the Opposition of being unable to accept the country's growth and movement towards self-reliance.He asserted that Indian democracy was strong and that citizens would unite to thwart attempts to destabilise the country.Why is CJP protesting at Jantar Mantar?The CJP has called for a demonstration demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and opposing the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.The protest comes amid an escalating political confrontation between the Opposition and the Election Commission of India over allegations of 'vote chori' and concerns surrounding the revision of electoral rolls.Delhi Police denied permission for the demonstration at Jantar Mantar, citing a previous breakdown of law and order in the area.CJP activist Abhijeet Dipke criticised the government's response to the planned protest, alleging that authorities were attempting to discourage people from participating.Speaking to reporters in Mumbai before leaving for Delhi, Dipke accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of being afraid of young people who question the government. He also alleged that police personnel were visiting residential areas to discourage residents from joining the demonstration.Dipke maintained that peaceful protest was a fundamental right under Article 19 of the Constitution.Delhi Metro closes gates at 45 stationsThe Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) announced restrictions at 45 Metro stations in view of the planned demonstration and the associated security arrangements.Entry and exit gates at the affected stations were closed from 9 pm on Friday, October 9, with the restrictions scheduled to continue through Saturday evening.The measures were intended to manage crowds and maintain security around sensitive locations in the national capital. The restrictions have also affected access to stations in areas surrounding the planned protest.Commuters have been advised to check official Delhi Metro updates before travelling, as services and access arrangements may change depending on the security situation.Delhi Airport issues travel advisoryDelhi Airport has advised passengers travelling to and from the airport to plan their journeys in advance and allow additional time for their commute.The advisory was issued amid heightened security arrangements and anticipated traffic restrictions linked to the protest.“In view of the enhanced security arrangements and anticipated traffic restrictions in Delhi, passengers travelling to and from Delhi Airport are advised to plan their journeys in advance and allow additional time for their commute,” the airport said in a statement.It also advised passengers to consider alternative transport options, including cabs and city buses, where appropriate.Delhi Traffic Police separately advised commuters to keep extra travel time if heading towards railway stations, inter-state bus terminals (ISBTs) or the airport through New Delhi and Central Delhi.People were also advised to avoid non-essential travel. The police said traffic management arrangements could be adjusted based on real-time assessments of the situation.Internet services suspended near Janpath and Kartavya PathAuthorities have imposed additional restrictions in parts of central Delhi, including a temporary suspension of internet services around the Janpath-Kartavya Path crossing.Internet services were suspended within a radius of 4 km from the crossing for 24 hours, starting at 10 pm on Friday, October 9.The area is considered sensitive because of its proximity to key government buildings and other important locations.Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) has also been imposed in Delhi as authorities step up security ahead of the demonstration.Separately, Gautam Buddh Nagar Police imposed prohibitory orders across the district from Saturday morning until October 20. The restrictions prohibit gatherings of five or more people without prior permission, processions, provocative speeches and the spread of misleading information.Security tightened at Delhi borders and key locationsDelhi Police remained on high alert on Saturday, with security strengthened across the national capital and vehicle checks intensified at inter-state and inter-district borders.Police personnel were deployed at several entry points, including the Aya Nagar, Ghazipur and Badarpur borders. Barricades were installed at multiple locations, while personnel checked vehicles entering Delhi.Deputy Commissioner of Police Anant Mittal visited the Aya Nagar border to review security arrangements.Speaking to news agency IANS, Mittal said special arrangements had been made at inter-state and inter-district borders to prevent unauthorised elements from entering New Delhi and to maintain law and order.Police personnel were also equipped with body cameras to record incidents and help monitor any physical altercations during the demonstration.Drone surveillance was underway at key locations, including New Delhi Railway Station, where Delhi Police and Rapid Action Force personnel were deployed. Security marches were also conducted.Security was strengthened outside the residences of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi. Additional security personnel were deployed at sensitive locations, while roads leading towards Janpath and Mandi House witnessed barricading and checks.Train cancellations inconvenience passengersSeveral trains were cancelled amid the heightened security arrangements, causing inconvenience to passengers travelling to and from Delhi on Saturday.Passengers at railway stations reported having to change their travel plans at short notice.One passenger told IANS that trains running via Jaunpur, including the Tapti Ganga and Kashi Vishwanath Express, had been cancelled. The passenger said they might have to travel to Lucknow and change trains or take a bus to reach their destination.Another passenger travelling from Gujarat said they had faced difficulties reaching Ghaziabad after arriving at Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station, as the expected connecting trains were unavailable.However, some passengers reported that their journeys had continued without difficulty, with trains arriving at Hazrat Nizamuddin on time.Police and Rapid Action Force personnel remained deployed at railway stations, while drone surveillance and security patrols continued.Delhi protest: What should commuters keep in mind?With security measures in force across Delhi and neighbouring areas, commuters should check the latest official advisories before setting out.Metro: Check DMRC updates for restrictions on entry and exit gates at affected stations.Airport: Allow extra time for travel and consider alternative transport options.Roads: Check Delhi Traffic Police advisories before travelling through central Delhi or towards railway stations and ISBTs.Trains: Verify train status with the relevant railway authorities before leaving for the station.Internet: Be aware of the reported temporary suspension of internet services in parts of central Delhi.Authorities have said that security and traffic arrangements may be modified depending on the situation on the ground. The restrictions come as police prepare to manage the planned demonstration while maintaining law and order across the national capital.

items.title: Amid reports of people filing bulk deletion requests, EC puts limits
items.summary:
Amid reports of people filing forms in bulk seeking removal of electors from voters lists, the Election Commission on Friday placed limits on individuals submitting such objections.
The EC has prescribed limits on the number of Form 7 applications an individual elector can file to object to the inclusion of names or seek deletion of names from electoral rolls.
During the claims and objections period, an individual elector can file a maximum of 10 Form 7 applications throughout the entire period.
During continuous updating of electoral rolls, the limit is five applications per month.
The move aims to discourage bulk filing of unsubstantiated objections, reduce inconvenience to voters and ease the workload of election officials.
The poll authority wrote to all state chief electoral officers to put in place the new system.

Sinner announced on Tuesday that he will miss the rest of the year due to knee inflammation. The five-time major winner has not played since July when he beat Alexander Zverev in the Wimbledon final. He then withdrew from the U.S. Open because of a right knee injury.
"I haven't been in touch with Jannik since he got injured, I just saw the news two days ago. So I'll reach out to him to see how he's doing," Djokovic said Thursday at the Shanghai Masters. "As someone that has been through some major injuries in my career."
For so long an ever-present on the ATP men's tour, Djokovic made the decision in late July 2017 to sit out the rest of that year after struggling with acute pain in his right elbow.

items.title: TCS unfazed by US PERM suspension
items.summary: Tata Consultancy Services, India's leading IT services company, said on Friday it does not expect its suspension from the permanent labour certification programme to impact either workforce strategy or customer engagements, adding that it would comply with any directive from the US Department of Labor.The US Labour Department on Thursday suspended eight major technology companies, including Indian software services exporters Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Infosys, Wipro, HCLTech, and Cognizant from the so-called permanent labour certification programme (PERM).Also Read: US suspends TCS, Infosys, Wipro, HCLTech, Cognizant and three other firms from PERM green card programmeThis effectively bars these firms from filing new applications or processing pending applications under the employment-based green card programme-after they have sponsored foreign workers on work visas such as H-1B. Capgemini, Microsoft and Adobe have also been suspended from the programme."Our workforce strategy in the US is anchored in hiring local talent, supported by a robust campus recruitment model. We have built a significant local workforce across 31 offices and delivery centers throughout the country," TCS said in a filing to exchanges.TCS added it was standing by its intention to hire 15,000 workers in the United States over the next five years, to improve its local workforce. The company added its PERM applications were in single digits in the last two years.Earlier, Microsoft reacted to the Donald Trump administration's immigration crackdown, post facing suspension from the Permanent Labour Certification Program, while the US President honoured the tech company's CEO Satya Nadella with the National Medal of Technology and Innovation.Microsoft highlighted that a huge majority of its US employees were Americans and stressed on its belief in the "strength and talent of the American workforce."

items.title: US to livestream Fort Hood shooter executive
items.summary: WASHINGTON, - The US will livestream the Army's upcoming firing squad execution on December 3 of Nidal Hasan, who killed 13 people at Fort Hood, Texas, in a 2009 shooting spree, a Pentagon official said, in what would be an unprecedented move.Hasan, a former Army psychiatrist, is set to become the first person to be executed by firing squad by the US military since 1945, shortly after the end of World War Two.The Pentagon official, who spoke on the condition of anonymity, did not offer more information and said details would follow.Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth earlier told the Human Events Daily podcast he planned to make Hasan's execution public, according to video of his comments posted on social media on Thursday.Hegseth said deciding to execute Hasan by firing squad at Fort Hood on a Thursday at 1 pm - the approximate time, day of the week and location of Hasan's shooting - was a "no brainer.""We'll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it's public. Because people need to understand that ... there's serious consequences for these types of things," Hegseth said.

GST reforms: No tax on toll collection
items.summary: In a move expected to settle tax ambiguity around highway monetisation and provide greater certainty to infrastructure projects, the GST Council on Thursday clarified that concessionaires collecting toll tax will have no tax exposure as the toll paid by users is exempt.The exemption will apply to both types of contracts, whether the concessionaire pays upfront or over time, and the two types of contracts will be treated alike, it said."If the toll itself bears no tax, the right to collect the toll cannot bear tax either, because the concessionaire is paying for nothing other than the toll he expects to collect," the council said.The council also said tax on road maintenance services will fall due when the concessionaire actually draws money against expenditure incurred, removing ambiguity over whether merely setting aside funds in an escrow account constitutes a tax liability. "The special procedure will be notified to give effect to this," it said.Under a national highway contract, a certain proportion of money is set aside in an escrow account for road maintenance and released only as it is spent.Kuljit Singh, partner and national infrastructure leader at EY India, said that in the absence of clarity on whether GST applied to toll collection, some risk-averse concessionaires were building the tax into their prices.

items.title: Surging bond yields likely to slash banks' treasury income
items.summary: Mumbai: Banks are expected to post a nearly 60% fall in treasury income for the July-September quarter from a year earlier due to a sharp increase in government bond yields.Analysts at Jefferies estimate aggregate treasury gains in the fiscal second quarter to be ₹5,500 crore, down 58% from ₹13,100 crore a year earlier. Sequentially, this income is expected to be 23% lower compared with ₹7,100 crore in the June quarter.The benchmark 10-year government bond yield rose about 44 basis points in the past quarter, ending September at around 7.19%, compared with roughly 6.75% three months prior. Five-year yields climbed by an even sharper 47 bps.Also Read | Deposit rate hikes unlikely for 3 months; RBI action to help NIMs: SBI chairman C S SettySince yields move inversely to bond prices, the sharp rise in yields has reversed the bond rally seen in the first quarter, when the 10-year yield fell about 28-32 bps. This reduced the scope for mark-to-market and trading gains on banks' investment portfolios, which form a major part of treasury income, and kept the profit growth muted in September quarter. "Treasury gains are expected to remain muted as bond yields have remained elevated," said Nitin Aggarwal of Motilal Oswal.134799550Bankers said the projection of a sharp YoY decline in treasury income also reflected a high base, as lenders had booked sizeable gains on their bond portfolios in the second quarter of last fiscal year. "Unless yields soften from current levels, treasury income is unlikely to provide the kind of earnings support that we saw last year. Profit growth over the next few quarters will increasingly have to come from core lending income, fee income and contained credit costs," said a senior treasury official at a private sector bank.Also Read |NBFC services to banks will attract 18% GSTThe impact is expected to be more pronounced for public sector banks, which typically have larger portfolios of government securities and had benefited from stronger treasury gains when bond yields softened in earlier quarters.

Home-cooked meals get 10% dearer in Sep on higher onion, oil, LPG prices
items.summary:
The cost of a home-cooked vegetarian thali rose 10 per cent year-on-year in September, driven by higher prices of onion, vegetable oil, rice and LPG, according to a report released on Thursday.
Non-vegetarian thali increased 6 per cent as broiler prices increased slower, according to Crisil's monthly Roti Rice Rate report.
The cost of preparing a vegetarian thali increased to Rs 30.8 in September from Rs 28.1 a year ago, while non-vegetarian thali cost rose to Rs 59.5 from Rs 56, the report said.

items.title: US probes top schools over J-1 visa use
items.summary: The United States has launched a federal investigation into nine major universities, including Ivy League schools like Harvard, Yale and Stanford over their use of J-1 visas, Vice President JD Vance said at a press briefing.The J-1 visa programme allows foreign nationals to enter the US as exchange visitors, including researchers, scholars, students, teachers and other specialists.Vance said Labor Department officials had served subpoenas on the universities as part of the investigation. He alleged that some institutions were bringing foreign researchers to the US at wages lower than those paid to American workers.Also Read| US bars Microsoft from sponsoring green cards for H-1B workers over alleged abuseThe universities named during the briefing included Harvard University, Yale University, Stanford University, the University of Pittsburgh, the University of California, Davis, the California Institute of Technology, Arizona State University and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.“We see a lot of fraud where some of America’s most universities bring in foreigners under the wages of American residents,” Vance said.He alleged that, in one case, a foreign researcher was paid $20,000 less than an American worker for a comparable position. Vance also referred to an example involving a salary difference of $48,000.“This is a terribly pernicious system. It’s gone for too long,” he said, calling for Congress and the administration to take steps to reform the programme.Vance said the J-1 visa programme was intended to give American institutions access to highly skilled researchers and professionals. However, he alleged that some employers were using it to reduce labour costs and replace American workers.“We cannot allow programmes that were designed to ensure that American corporations had access to the best and the brightest to be used to undercut the wages of workers,” Vance said.He also distinguished between foreign workers who come to the US to build companies and create jobs, and those whom employers allegedly bring in at lower wages to replace American workers.“If you want the visa programme to stop being used to defraud the taxpayer and undercut the wages of workers, we will help you do everything that we can to ensure the programme was designed for America,” Vance said.

items.title: EV sales in America and Europe
items.summary: US car shoppers have been slow to warm back up to electric vehicles since a key federal subsidy expired a year ago, despite persistently high gas prices, while Europeans have flocked to the cars.EV sales in the US are down 30.7% this year through September, according to research firm Motor Intelligence, accounting for just 6% of overall sales. That's less than the 8.5% at this time a year ago, when buyers rushed to beat the expiration of a $7,500 federal tax credit.In Europe, however, buyers have flocked to electrics for relief from higher fuel prices stemming from the war in Iran. EVs accounted for 23.2% of the European auto market this year through September, up from 17.7% a year earlier, according to the European Automobile Manufacturers' Association.Read more: Trev plans 2,500-vehicle premium EV fleet by 2031, raising $2 millionThe divergence in the two markets is due in part to key policy differences between the two regions. In Europe, automakers continue to roll out electric models to meet stringent tailpipe-emissions regulations, and Chinese automakers have stormed the European market with a slew of imported EVs.In the US, the Trump administration worked with Congress to eliminate support for EVs, and watered down fuel-efficiency regulations. High tariffs and a ban on Chinese-made vehicle software have effectively blocked Chinese car brands.Meanwhile, there were more than 150 EVs on sale in Europe during the first half of 2026, up from about 100 models in 2024, according to Transport & Environment, a Brussels-based environmental advocacy group. Many are priced below 25,000 euros ($27,995), and many countries offer tax breaks to lower consumers' out-of-pocket costs.Read more: India luxury car sales rise 10% in 2026 as Mercedes-Benz, BMW see strong EV demandUS BUYERS GO FOR HYBRIDS, USED EVSSince the expiration of the $7,500 federal tax credit a year ago, many US automakers have discontinued electric models or scrapped plans for new entries. Some have done away with cheap leases that helped fuel demand.Buyers instead are seeking hybrids and used EVs, car dealers and analysts say. Hybrid sales jumped 23% through the first three quarters from the year-earlier period, accounting for 15.6% of total sales over that stretch."There's still demand out there [for EVs], but the energy and the masses are definitely running to hybrid technology," said Thad Szott, a Detroit-area dealer with Ford, Stellantis and Toyota.Some automakers are adding hybrids to their showrooms. Nissan, for example, moved up the launch of a new hybrid system on its popular Rogue SUV by several months.Hybrids are "a safer choice" for consumers worried about driving range, said Tiago Castro, Nissan's senior vice president of US marketing and sales. "When we had the government incentive" for EVs, he said, "it was a different story."The market for used EVs is bustling, though, a sign that less affluent buyers are seeking relief from high fuel prices. Sales of used electric cars rose 19% through September from the year-earlier period, according to research site CarGurus.TESLA, RIVIAN EVS FARE BETTER THAN LEGACY CARMAKERSEV-only brands have fared better than traditional automakers' EV sales. Tesla's US sales fell only 14% in the first three quarters, a milder decline than the broader electric vehicle market, according to an estimate from Motor Intelligence. Rivian's US sales rose 29%, helped by the release of a new SUV, the R2.By contrast, Ford's EV sales are down 68% this year through September, while crosstown rival General Motors saw a 43% drop in EV sales.Honda has opted to end production of its EVs after this year, while planning to expand hybrid sales. "Once they scaled back the $7,500, it became obvious" that EV market share would decline, said Lance Woelfer, vice president of US auto sales at Honda.However, South Korean automaker Hyundai has seen some recovery in EV sales since gas prices began rising in late winter, and dealers are asking for them, said Randy Parker, CEO of Hyundai Motor North America."We're not giving up on EVs by any stretch of the imagination," Parker said.

items.title: Deposit rates unlikely to rise for upto 3 months: SBI chairman Setty
items.summary:
State Bank of India Chairman C S Setty on Thursday said he does not see deposit rate hike for up to three months because of the excess liquidity in the system.
Speaking a day after the RBI's policy announcement, Setty said the shift to tightening of rates by the central bank will help banks expand their net interest margins (NIMs) for up to three quarters.
"I believe that next two-three months, there may not be any rate action on the deposits because we have sufficient liquidity in the system," Setty told reporters here.
He, however, added that if the credit growth continues at the ongoing elevated levels, some banks may have to look at raising deposit rates to fund the advances.
Setty also acknowledged that depositors need to be compensated with some level of positive real interest rate in a scenario where inflation is inching up.

Air India will offer travel SIM cards to passengers for their overseas trips.
EasyRoam,  an Air India-branded travel SIM card that offers international roaming services, has been developed in partnership with Tata Communications.
The ancillary product will be available for purchase as a physical SIM card as well as eSIM on a dedicated Air India-branded webpage, the airline said in a release on Thursday.
With the card, passengers will be able to access voice and data services during international travel.
Air India and Tata Communications are part of the Tata Group.
Initially, the SIM card will be provided free of cost while roaming pack charges will apply.
It will be available for 30 countries across North America, Europe (including the UK), Australia, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East, the release said.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday called for a global framework to tackle cyber frauds and deepfakes, saying digital threats have crossed national boundaries and require coordinated action by all stakeholders.
Inaugurating the tenth edition of the India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026, Modi said governments, technology companies, telecom operators and financial institutions should create mechanisms to curb digital frauds.
"I urge the GSMA and telecom operators across the world: come, let us create a global mechanism that can stop such fraud before it reaches the people. India has learnt a lot from its experiences in this direction, and India is always ready to share its experiences with the world," Modi said.
Technology can achieve scale only when it gains people's trust, he said.
A person sitting in one country, with the help of a person in another country, can commit a crime in a third country, Modi said, adding that deepfakes have become a big challenge.

India aims to double its 5G user base from 550 million to one billion by 2030, Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia said on Thursday, adding that the country, which was behind the world in 4G, has resolved to lead the world in 6G.
Speaking at the inauguration of the 10th edition of the India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026, Scindia said 5G in India has become the fastest-adopted 5G technology in the world.
"Today we have 550 million users on 5G...But we will not rest here. By 2030 our target is to take that number from 550 million to a billion customers on 5G," he said.
On 6G, Scindia said the Bharat 6G Alliance, which has 90 institutions involved with it, has established 7,700 patents, of which 4,400 are international.
"We were behind the world in 4G. We marched with the world on 5G. But it is our resolve that we will lead the world on 6G," he said.

The rupee traded in a narrow range and edged up 10 paise to 96.65 against US dollar in early trade on Thursday on likely intervention by the  Reserve Bank of India.
Forex traders said rupee is under pressure amid persistent macroeconomic headwinds, including global dollar strength (DXY trading near multi-month highs), elevated Brent crude prices hovering near USD 102 per barrel.
Moreover, relentless foreign fund outflows as well as fall in forex reserves by USD 50 billion in just three weeks from the high of USD 786 billion in September dented investor sentiments further.
At the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 96.71, then gained some ground to touch 96.65, registering a rise of 10 paise over its previous close.
On Wednesday, the rupee closed at 96.75 against the American currency.

The Ebola outbreak in Congo is creating new hot spots where there's little to no support for patients, responders and officials say, as health workers admit there could still be a long way to go in fighting the disease that has killed over 4,000 people.
More than 70 per cent of new cases are still coming from outside of known contacts and at least 60 per cent of deaths are outside of treatment centers, Africa CDC Director-General Dr. Jean Kaseya told The Associated Press. "There are so many other people who are becoming sick, who are not tested, treated, or listed," said Kaseya on Tuesday.
The conflict-battered, remote North Kivu province, which has emerged as the new epicentre, now accounts for around 40% of all newly confirmed cases in Congo, compared with 24% at the end of August. items.summary: Wall Street cooled off, with the Dow falling 0.7%, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq declined 0.2% each, pulling back from their all-time highs. Treasury yields spiked again, with the US 10-year yield rising to 5.36% intraday, its highest level since 2002, while the 30-year yield touched 5.73%, a fresh 24-year high. Yields retraced from their peaks after a successful $39 billion US Treasury auction. September FOMC minutes showed that a majority of policymakers backed one more rate hike by the end of 2026. The dollar held on to its gains, with the Dollar Index rising 0.4% to 102.26, while Brent crude edged higher towards $101 a barrel as the IEA agreed to release diesel reserves on priority. Asian markets are trading lower, while Gift Nifty indicates a cautious start. In India, the market snapped its two-day gaining streak, with the Nifty slipping back below 22,700 as the RBI’s 25-basis-point rate hike and cautious commentary weighed on sentiment. The rupee weakened against the dollar, slipping to a five-month low of 96.78 per dollar. FIIs were net sellers of ₹6,121.37 crore in equities, while DIIs were net buyers of ₹4,596.57 crore.

Later, the Delhi High Court ordered that Paytm Payments Bank Ltd (PPBL) be wound up.

Gold prices fell for the second straight session, declining Rs 700 to Rs 1.48 lakh per 10 grams in the national capital on Wednesday, as subdued local demand and weak global trend weighed on the precious metal.
The yellow metal of 99.9 per cent purity fell to a one-week low, depreciating Rs 700 to Rs 1,48,900 per 10 grams, inclusive of all taxes, from Tuesday's closing level of Rs 1,49,600, according to local traders.
It was quoted at Rs 1,48,600 per 10 grams on September 29.
"Gold prices declined in the domestic market on Wednesday amid weak global cues and subdued retail demand," said Saumil Gandhi, Senior Analyst - Commodities at HDFC Securities.
A rebound in crude oil amid renewed concerns over supply disruptions triggered by West Asia tensions also added to the dip in the precious metal prices, he added.
However, depreciation in the rupee kept a lid on the precious metal's upside, analysts said.

items.title: Delhi HC judge recuses self from hearing Gymkhana Club eviction case
items.summary:
Delhi High Court judge Justice Prateek Jalan on Wednesday recused himself from hearing a lawsuit over the Centre's proceedings against the Delhi Gymkhana Club for its eviction from the 27.3-acre premises on Safdarjung Road here.
Justice Jalan directed that the lawsuit by the Delhi Gymkhana Club Ltd Staff Welfare Association be listed before another bench on Friday.
"I am going to recuse from this matter. There are matters where one does not trust one's own judgement," Justice Jalan said.
"There is too much personal involved. I will feel more comfortable of someone else heard it," he further observed.
Gymkhana member Vijay Khurana and Delhi Gymkhana Club Ltd Staff Welfare Association have filed separate lawsuits against the Land and Development Office (L&DO)'s May 22 order terminating the colonial-era club's perpetual lease deed and asking it to return its land by June 5 on grounds of "strengthening and securing defence infrastructure".
Khurana's lawsuit is stated to be supported .

items.title: Live: Banks, realty, auto stocks slip on RBI's hawkish shift; rupee crosses 97/$ | Closing Bell
items.summary: Markets break down after the RBI’s rate hike, with the central bank raising rates by 25 basis points after nearly four years and switching its stance to “calibrated tightening”. The RBI raises its FY27 growth forecast by 40 basis points to 7.1%, while the FY27 inflation forecast is increased by 20 basis points to 5.2%. The Sensex slips over 400 points, while the Nifty falls 250 points. The rupee breaches the 97-per-dollar mark, weakening 60 paise, while India’s 10-year bond yield rises to 7.2%. Market breadth turns negative, with declines outnumbering advances, and barring PSU banks, all sectors come under pressure. The Bank Nifty trims its losses and remains 450 points off the day’s low. Metal stocks decline sharply as the Dollar Index moves above 102, while auto and realty stocks fall following the rate action. Broader markets remain mixed, with smallcaps outperforming. Among Nifty 50 stocks, Kotak Mahindra Bank, Bharti Airtel and BSE are the top gainers, while Titan, JSW Steel and Adani Enterprises are the top losers.

items.title: Son Heung-min surpasses Cha Bum to become top goal scorer for South Korea
items.summary:
Son Heung-min became South Korea's all-time leading scorer when his 59th goal helped the team beat Uzbekistan 2-0 in a friendly on Tuesday.
The sixth-minute free kick moved Son past Cha Bum-kun's record of 58. Cha retired from international soccer after the 1986 World Cup.
Oh Se-hun added a second goal on the hour as South Korea won comfortably at Mireu Stadium in Yongin, about 40 kilometers (25 miles) south of Seoul.
Son also holds South Korea's appearance record with 151 caps. He made his international debut in 2010 and has played at four World Cups.
The 34-year-old joined Los Angeles FC in 2025 after a decade with Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League.
The win ended a mixed international break for South Korea and interim coach Robert Moreno. The team beat Ecuador 3-0, lost to Uruguay 4-1 and drew with Venezuela 0-0.
South Korea and Uzbekistan are preparing for the 2027 Asian Cup which kicks off in Saudi Arabia on Jan. 7.

items.title: Delhi High Court judge strength rises to 50 after new appointment
items.summary:
The Delhi High Court on Wednesday got a new judge with the swearing-in of Justice Gurvinder Pal Singh.
Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre administered the oath of office to Justice Singh, taking the strength of judges of the Delhi High Court to 50.
The sanctioned strength of the high court is 60 which includes 45 permanent and 15 additional judges.
The swearing-in ceremony was held in the high court premises.
Justice Singh, who was a judicial officer of the Delhi district judiciary and has been elevated to the high court as an additional judge, took oath in Hindi.
The Centre had on October 5 notified the appointment of the judicial officer as judge of the high court.
In September, a total of seven judges had taken the oath of the office of the Delhi High Court.
On September 10, the Supreme Court Collegium had recommended eight judicial officers for elevation to the Delhi High Court.
While seven were elevated, Singh did not find his name in that list.

items.title: RBI MPC Key Takeaways: Repo rate up to 5.50%
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), headed by Governor Sanjay Malhotra, raised the policy repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% on Wednesday, marking its first rate hike since February 2023, as rising crude oil prices, food inflation and weather-related risks clouded the inflation outlook.The RBI also raised its FY27 GDP growth forecast to 7.1% from 6.7% and its inflation projection to 5.2% from 5.1%, while shifting its policy stance to calibrated tightening.The MPC voted unanimously to increase the repo rate, while the decision to change the policy stance to calibrated tightening was taken by a majority of 4-2.Also read: RBI Policy Meeting 2026 Live: Malhotra & co hikes repo rate by 25 bps to 5.50% as war creeps into Indian retail inflation; more rate cuts off the table in near termHere are the key takeaways from the RBI MPC meeting:1. Repo rate raised by 25 bps to 5.50%The MPC unanimously voted to raise the policy repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%, the first increase since February 2023. The Standing Deposit Facility rate now stands at 5.25%, while the Marginal Standing Facility rate and the bank rate have been adjusted to 5.75%.The rate hike comes amid renewed inflationary pressures from rising international crude oil prices, higher food prices and an uneven monsoon. The RBI also flagged the challenging global environment, marked by geopolitical tensions, trade uncertainty and volatility in financial markets.“The MPC noted that the global context, on account of geopolitical developments, remains challenging. Nonetheless, the Indian economy has been strong, and the economic momentum remains broad based,” Malhotra said.2. FY27 GDP growth forecast raised to 7.1%The RBI raised its real GDP growth projection for FY27 to 7.1% from 6.7%, an upward revision of 40 basis points, reflecting the resilience of domestic economic activity.The central bank projected growth at 7.2% for the second quarter, 6.9% for the third quarter and 6.8% for the fourth quarter of FY27. Real GDP growth for the first quarter of FY28 is projected at 7.1%.The RBI said high-frequency indicators for the second quarter pointed to sustained economic momentum, supported by steady services activity, manufacturing resilience, domestic demand and investment. Both manufacturing and services purchasing managers’ indices remained in expansionary territory.However, global economic uncertainty, supply-chain disruptions, elevated commodity prices and geopolitical tensions could weigh on the outlook. A weak southwest monsoon and strong El Niño conditions could also affect the upcoming rabi season and rural demand.Also read: RBI Inflation FY2026-27: Malhotra & Co raises inflation forecast to 5.2% for FY273. FY27 inflation forecast raised to 5.2%The RBI raised its CPI inflation forecast for FY27 to 5.2% from 5.1%, reflecting persistent price pressures from food and fuel.Retail inflation rose to 4.8% in August from 4.5% in July, driven largely by higher food and fuel inflation. The central bank also flagged a broadening of price pressures across food commodities and early signs of inflation becoming more generalised.The RBI projected CPI inflation at 4.9% for the second quarter, 6% for the December quarter and 5.7% for the fourth quarter of FY27. Inflation for the first quarter of FY28 is projected at 5.6%, with risks evenly balanced. Core inflation for FY27 is projected at 4.4%.The central bank highlighted the risks posed by volatile international oil prices, deficient and uneven monsoon rainfall and El Niño conditions, which could affect agricultural output and food prices.4. MPC shifts stance to calibrated tightening; rate cuts off the tableThe MPC changed its policy stance to calibrated tightening by a majority of 4-2, signalling a sharper focus on containing inflationary pressures.The central bank said inflation and its outlook were no longer as benign as they had been in the previous year. While there was some evidence of elevated inflation expectations and a generalisation of price pressures, the RBI noted limited signs of supply-side pressures becoming embedded in pricing behaviour.The governor underscored that rate cuts were no longer an option in the near term.“Given the current conditions, rate cuts are off the table in the near term, and policy action ahead can only be a rate hike or a pause, depending on the evolving conditions and the outlook,” Malhotra said.The duration and extent of any rate-hike cycle, he added, would depend on actual growth and inflation developments, underlying inflation, the broadening of price pressures and the second-round effects of supply shocks.5. Liquidity remains in surplus; RBI to align call rate with policy rateSystem liquidity increased substantially over the previous two months following measures undertaken to attract capital inflows. The average daily surplus liquidity, measured by the net position under the liquidity adjustment facility, stood at ₹5.9 lakh crore since the previous MPC meeting.Subsequent liquidity-absorption measures and quarterly advance-tax outflows moderated the surplus somewhat in September. The weighted average call rate largely traded in the lower half of the policy corridor, while short-term money-market rates moderated significantly.The RBI said it would continue using an appropriate mix of liquidity-management tools to align the weighted average call rate with the policy repo rate.6. RBI announces measures on account aggregation and financial marketsThe RBI announced two additional measures alongside its monetary policy decisions.First, it will allow interoperability among non-banking financial company account aggregators, enabling users to aggregate financial information across different account aggregators by onboarding with just one.Second, the central bank will facilitate SEBI-regulated depositories in including bank deposit account information in consolidated account statements. This will allow individuals to access information on bank deposits alongside their securities, equity and debt holdings in a consolidated statement. The measures are to be implemented by the end of 2026.The RBI will also constitute a technical consultative committee for financial markets to provide a forum for structured engagement with market participants and other stakeholders on policy and operational matters.
